### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 runs in about 70 in 100 cases, up from about 19 in 100 (mean occurrences per trace about 0.78 versus 0.21), and it now appears near the start of the case: its mean relative position fell from about 0.55 to about 0.19 (median about 0.34 to 0.15). These are event positions, not clock times. [OCC003, POS001]
- Before, A10 co-occurred with each of A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A31, A32, A47 and A48 in only about 19 in 100 cases — those activities usually ran without it (about 81 in 100) — and it came first in only about 9–17 in 100 cases, with no consistent order; in the later window A10 co-occurs with each in about 70 in 100 cases (about 48 in 100 for A45 and A46, up from about 16 in 100) and comes first in about 60–62 in 100 cases for each partner. [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- A10's immediate neighbourhood changed: A14 precedes A10 in about 60 in 100 cases (previously about 17 in 100), and the succession is now almost always immediate — a one-step gap in about 98 in 100 of 133 observed pairs, versus mixed gaps across 11 pairs before; A10 in turn precedes A15 in about 38 in 100 cases, with about 30 in 100 interleaved (before, A15 usually preceded A10), and the A14→A15 gap shifted from one to two steps, consistent with A10 now sitting between them. [REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- The fixed internal order of the group A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 dissolved: before, each of A20, A22 and A23 preceded each of A24, A25 and A26 in about 96–99 in 100 cases; in the later window A24 usually precedes A20 (about 74 in 100) and A23 (about 85 in 100), A26 usually precedes A23 (about 67 in 100), A20–A26, A22–A24 and A23–A25 appear in both orders in near-equal shares, and A20–A25 and A22–A26 keep only weakened majorities (about 68 and 75 in 100). Relative positions moved the same way: A20, A22 and A23 shifted later, A24, A25 and A26 earlier. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Fixed spacing loosened across the sequence: successions that had one dominant gap now spread over one to five steps — e.g., A22 immediately before A20 in 100 in 100 observed pairs before versus about 56 in 100 after; A20 immediately before A23 in about 99 in 100 versus about 68 in 100; A20 to A25 four steps apart in all observed pairs before, now spread over one to four steps; A31's fixed gaps to A20, A22, A23, A24 and A26 spread the same way. [LAG004, LAG006, LAG009, LAG010, LAG012, LAG025, LAG026, LAG027, LAG028, LAG029]
- A04 and A08 became rarer (participation about 21 → 11 and about 20 → 4 in 100 cases); A15's position shifted slightly later (mean about 0.17 → 0.19); A47→A48 tightened to a one-step gap in about 99 in 100 pairs (from about 87 in 100), and A45→A48 concentrated on a three-step gap (about 83 in 100, from about 51 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, POS002, LAG031, LAG032]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A10's role changed: in the later window A10 is a frequent, early-executed activity — running in about 70 in 100 cases (previously about 19 in 100), placed near the start of the case, typically immediately preceded by A14, preceding each of A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 in about 60 in 100 cases (previously about 9–10 in 100, with no fixed order), and followed within one step by A15 in about half of the observed successions — whereas in the earlier window A10 was a rare, mid-trace activity that usually ran without those activities. Occurrence, position, relation and lag indicators all describe this same shift, each difference being larger than what about 995 of 1000 random re-splits produce, and the volume of qualifying evidence (65 items against fewer than one expected without change) cannot be explained by chance sampling. [OCC003, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

The evidence cannot distinguish a rerouting within one process from a shift in the mix of case variants between the windows; it also does not show which activities now fill the widened gaps between the group's members, and "earlier" refers to event positions rather than clock time. [LAG006, LAG012, POS001]

Other differences:

- The ordering constraints inside the group dissolved, independently of A10's new position: the strict sequence in which A20, A22 and A23 each preceded A24, A25 and A26 (about 96–99 in 100 cases) gave way to usually reversed pairs (A24 before A20 in about 74 in 100; A24 before A23 in about 85 in 100; A26 before A23 in about 67 in 100), near-symmetric mixed pairs (A20–A26, A22–A24, A23–A25) and weakened majorities (A20 before A25 about 68 in 100; A22 before A26 about 75 in 100), while the previously fixed gaps between group members and from A31 and A32 spread over one to five steps. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG004, LAG006, LAG008, LAG010, LAG012, LAG016, LAG019, LAG025, LAG028]
- A04 and A08 became rarer, running in about 11 and 4 in 100 cases respectively (previously about 21 and 20 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002]
- A15's position moved slightly later (mean relative position about 0.17 → 0.19), A47→A48 became an almost universal one-step succession (about 99 in 100 pairs, from about 87 in 100), and A45→A48 concentrated on a three-step gap (about 83 in 100, from about 51 in 100). [POS002, LAG031, LAG032]
